title: Portainer — What it is
description: Portainer is a lightweight management interface for containerized environments: it turns Docker, Docker Swarm and Kubernetes clusters into clickable dashboards where containers, images, volumes, networks and stacks can be started, stopped, inspected and logged without memorizing CLI flags. For an AI workstation it is the visual control room over local model servers, vector databases and inference microservices. The Community Edition is free and deploys as a single container itself. It is made by Portainer.io and runs on Any host running Docker (Linux, Windows, macOS via Docker Desktop).
facts: The web UI is served over HTTPS on port 9443 by default.
Stacks deploy multi-container apps from docker-compose files pasted into the UI.
One Portainer instance can manage many remote Docker hosts (endpoints).

From there the demo below walks a first-run checklist so a new user goes from zero to a working setup in minutes, not hours.

title: Portainer — Configuration essentials
description: Portainer is configured through a small, explicit surface: `portainer.port`, `portainer.endpoint`, `portainer.auto_update`, `portainer.https_only`. The demo below validates a sample configuration against the required keys, because most Portainer failures are configuration mistakes, and a validator catches them before they cost time.
facts: One Portainer instance can manage many remote Docker hosts (endpoints).
It manages Docker, Swarm and Kubernetes from the same dashboard.
Container logs, stats, console access and image pulls are all available in the UI.
demo_code:
required = ['portainer.port', 'portainer.endpoint', 'portainer.auto_update', 'portainer.https_only']
sample = {
    'portainer.port': 9443,
    'portainer.endpoint': 'local docker.sock',
    'portainer.auto_update': False,
    'portainer.https_only': True,
}
print('CONFIG VALIDATION')
ok = True
for k in required:
    good = k in sample and sample[k] not in (None, '')
    ok = ok and good
    print(f"  [{'PASS' if good else 'FAIL'}] {k} = {sample.get(k)!r}")
print('RESULT:', 'valid configuration' if ok else 'INVALID')

title: Portainer — Troubleshooting
description: When Portainer misbehaves, diagnose in order: re-check configuration, re-run the entry command `docker run -d -p 9443:9443 --name portainer --restart=always -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -v portainer_data:/data portainer/portainer-ce:latest` (install Portainer CE), then inspect the data formats for corruption. The demo below encodes this decision tree so the most common failures resolve to a concrete next step.
facts: Portainer Community Edition is free and open source.
It installs as a single Docker container mounting the host Docker socket.
The web UI is served over HTTPS on port 9443 by default.
demo_code:
tree = [("won't start", 're-run entry command: docker run -d -p 9443:9443 --name portainer --restart=always -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock -v portainer_data:/data portainer/portainer-ce:latest (install Portainer CE)'), ('wrong behavior', 'validate config keys: portainer.port, portainer.endpoint, portainer.auto_update'), ("can't find data", 'check docker-compose YAML (stacks) files exist in expected paths'), ('slow', 'reduce scope, then consult performance record (ladder 13)')]
symptom = 'wrong behavior'
print('DIAGNOSTIC DECISION TREE')
for s, fix in tree:
    mark = '>>>' if s == symptom else '   '
    print(f'{mark} if {s}: {fix}')
print('diagnosis for', repr(symptom), '->', [f for s, f in tree if s == symptom][0])
